subject: Contractor onboarding & authz patterns for Private Control Plane
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Ng <lisa.ng@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contractor onboarding & authz patterns for Private Control Plane

Hi Lisa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I've sketched three pragmatic patterns for contractor access to a Private Control Plane deployed inside Acme's VPC. Goal: keep blast radius small, satisfy your procurement & audit needs, and minimize ongoing ops for your team.

High-level options (tradeoffs in short):
- Scoped Contractor Accounts: issue contractor-specific SAML assertions mapped to limited role(s). Pros: clear audit trail; Cons: more IdP mapping work.
- Proxy Operator Pool: contractors access via a small operator pool (jumpbox/service account) with short-lived sessions and explicit approvals. Pros: minimal IdP changes; Cons: operational overhead and less granular per-contractor auditing.
- Delegated Access with SCIM Groups: manage contractors as a group in IdP (SCIM-managed) with time-bound entitlements. Pros: scalable lifecycle; Cons: requires SCIM provisioning from Acme side.

Questions for you:
1) Which of the above aligns better with your contractor procurement / audit language?
2) Do you have a preference for per-contractor identities vs shared operator pool?
3) Any restrictions on bringing a SCIM connector (we can support OIDC + SCIM or SAML + SCIM)?

Attached: a starter role matrix CSV and a short checklist for onboarding (PDF). I also attached a rough SAML assertion mapping diagram.

Next step: if you confirm preferred pattern, we can produce an Operator Playbook (1-2 pages) and a small runbook for your SREs. Jordan/Ben — can you add any implementation constraints from our private control plane for the chosen pattern?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

Attachments: acme-contractor-role-matrix.csv (text/csv), onboarding-checklist.pdf (application/pdf), saml-assertion-mapping-v2.png (image/png)
From: Lisa Ng <lisa.ng@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Rogers <kyle.rogers@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contractor onboarding & authz patterns for Private Control Plane

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers: 
- Audit needs: we need per-contractor identity where feasible. Procurement will not accept long-lived shared creds unless there's compensating controls.
- SCIM: we have SCIM enabled in our IdP (Okta) but procurement requires us to run it through Security for an outbound connector — possible but will add a 2-3 week approval window.
- SAML/OIDC: SAML is our default for legacy apps; new integrations often prefer OIDC. If you support either, we can map to our IdP team.

Immediate ask: can Redwood provide an "operator approval" flow as a fallback (e.g., temporary elevation by a named Acme admin) while our SCIM connector is approved? That would let us onboard contractors gradually. Also — what field in the SAML assertion would you recommend we use for contractor role mapping? (we currently send group membership and an "employeeType" attribute).

Cc'ing Kyle from infrastructure and procurement so they see the constraints.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Ng
IT Security Lead, Acme Corporation
lisa.ng@acme.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Ng <lisa.ng@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contractor onboarding & authz patterns for Private Control Plane

Lisa — great context, thank you. Summary / proposed path: 
1) Short-term (2 weeks): Scoped Contractor Accounts via SAML + Attribute Mapping. We will accept Okta SAML assertions with a mapped attribute (recommended: employeeType = "contractor" and groups for fine-grain roles). We'll provide a sample assertion and an assertion validation script to speed Security review.

2) Fallback while SCIM is approved: Operator Approval Flow — we can enable an admin-initiated temporary session flow. Key controls:
   - 15-minute session tokens, multi-admin approval (2/2) for elevation to operator pool
   - All operator actions audited and streamed to your SIEM (we will support a syslog/HTTPS delivery)
   - Auto-revocation after 24 hours unless renewed by the named Acme admin

3) Medium-term (recommended): SCIM-managed groups for contractors with time-bound membership (e.g., 30-day default). Once SCIM is enabled, we can automate deprovisioning.

Jordan/Ben — implementation constraints / infra notes:
- Jordan: are there IP allowlist considerations for the operator pool? Can we restrict temporary sessions to Acme-managed jumpbox IPs?
- Ben: we need a minimal SAML metadata template from Acme and your security checklist so we can pre-populate the assertion validator. Also any HSM/KMS notes for on-prem key wrapping?

Laura

> Laura — quick note on IPs: we support per-tenant CIDR allowlists in the private control plane. For temporary operator sessions we can gate by those ranges. If Acme wants to restrict to jumpbox IPs, we'll enforce at the control-plane ingress.

> Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Contractor onboarding & authz patterns for Private Control Plane

Lisa / team — following internal sync, proposed deliverables & decisions ready for your review: 

Deliverables (next steps):
- Operator Playbook (1 page): shows approval flow, admin contacts, and session durations — attached as PDF (see onboarding-checklist.pdf).
- SAML Assertion Example + Validator: small script + metadata (we'll provide a sandbox endpoint for assertion testing).
- Temporary Operator Pool: config change on your Private CP instance; we'll coordinate a 2-hour maintenance window to enable and test.

Decisions we need from Acme: 
1) Approve temporary operator approval flow as compensating control while SCIM connector is approved (we recommend 2-admin approval).
2) Confirm the SAML attribute to use for mapping (employeeType vs groups). We recommend using employeeType=contractor AND a groups attribute for role mapping.
3) Confirm the CIDR(s) or jumpbox IPs to pin temporary sessions to (send to jordan.blake@redwood.com).

Security notes: all operator actions will be audited; we can push logs to your SIEM (we need endpoint + shared secret). For HSM/KMS: if you require CMEK for control-plane secrets, we can document the integration (there will be a small ops lead time).

Please reply with 1/2/3 above and we'll schedule the maintenance window.

Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
